mathleague-2004-05-g8-01.title: Subtract 1000
mathleague-2004-05-g8-01.body:
Subtracting 1000 from both numbers on the left gives $110-20=90$. Then $110-20=110-?$ gives $?=20$.

**Answer: (D) 20**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-02.title: Side then area
mathleague-2004-05-g8-02.body:
Each side is $4\div4=1$, so the area is $1^2=1$.

**Answer: (A) 1**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-04.title: Definition
mathleague-2004-05-g8-04.body:
Five-fourths is $\frac54$. Choice (B) is a mixed number and (C) a decimal; only (D) is an improper fraction.

**Answer: (D) $\frac54$**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-06.title: Convert
mathleague-2004-05-g8-06.body:
120 seconds is 2 minutes, so the time is 12:02 A.M.

**Answer: (B) 12:02 A.M.**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-10.title: List them
mathleague-2004-05-g8-10.body:
The one-digit primes are 2, 3, 5, 7 (1 is not prime). Their sum is $17$.

**Answer: (C) 17**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-12.title: All angles are equal
mathleague-2004-05-g8-12.body:
Let the angles be $x,y,z$. Then $x+y=y+z=x+z=120^\circ$, so $x=y=z$. Each angle is $60^\circ$ (check: $3\times60=180$). The triangle is equiangular.

**Answer: (D) equiangular**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-13.title: Alternate days
mathleague-2004-05-g8-13.body:
Cloudy days cannot be next to each other. Taking Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday as cloudy gives 4 days.

**Answer: (B) 4**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-13.title: Upper bound
mathleague-2004-05-g8-13.body:
Split the 7 days into the pairs (Sun, Mon), (Tue, Wed), (Thu, Fri) and the single day Sat. Each pair holds at most one cloudy day, so there are at most $3+1=4$ cloudy days.

**Answer: (B) 4**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-14.title: Evaluate
mathleague-2004-05-g8-14.body:
$(-1)^2=1$, $(-2)^2=4$, $(-3)^2=9$, and the first choice is 7. The largest is 9.

**Answer: (D) $(-3)^2$**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-16.title: Compare in cents
mathleague-2004-05-g8-16.body:
The dealer paid 50 cents per egg and sold it for $50\times25=1250$ cents. Bunny got $\frac{50}{1250}=\frac{4}{100}=4\%$.

**Answer: (B) 4%**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-17.title: Use powers
mathleague-2004-05-g8-17.body:
$256=2^8$. Each square root halves the exponent: $2^8\to2^4\to2^2\to2^1=2$.

**Answer: (A) 2**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-20.title: Locate between fifths
mathleague-2004-05-g8-20.body:
The fifths near 0.33 are $\frac15=0.2$ and $\frac25=0.4$. Since $0.4-0.33=0.07<0.13=0.33-0.2$, the nearest is $\frac25$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac25$**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-21.title: Pennies first
mathleague-2004-05-g8-21.body:
Every coin except pennies is worth a multiple of 5¢, so the number of pennies leaves remainder 4 when divided by 5: it is 4 (9 pennies would be too many for 7 coins). The other 3 coins are worth 45¢, which is only possible as a quarter and 2 dimes. There are no nickels.

**Answer: (A) 0**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-22.title: Convert to metres
mathleague-2004-05-g8-22.body:
$60\text{ cm}=0.6\text{ m}$ and $0.02\text{ km}=20\text{ m}$. The sum is $1.5+0.6+20=22.1\text{ m}$.

**Answer: (C) 22.1 m**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-23.title: Factor 222
mathleague-2004-05-g8-23.body:
$222=2\times3\times37$. The even factors are 2 times a factor of 111: $2\times\{1,3,37,111\}=2,6,74,222$. That is 4 factors.

**Answer: (B) 4**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-24.title: Middle value
mathleague-2004-05-g8-24.body:
The numbers $1,2,\ldots,99$ are evenly spaced, so the average equals the middle number, 50.

**Answer: (D) 50.00**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-25.title: Radii
mathleague-2004-05-g8-25.body:
If the large radius is $R$, the small radius is $\frac R2$. Areas scale with the square of the radius, so the ratio is $\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac14=25\%$.

**Answer: (B) 25**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-26.title: Unit rate
mathleague-2004-05-g8-26.body:
$\frac13$ cup feeds 4 fish, so 1 cup feeds 12 fish, and 4 cups feed $48$ fish.

**Answer: (D) 48**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-26.title: Ratio
mathleague-2004-05-g8-26.body:
$4\div\frac23=6$, so 4 cups is 6 times as much as $\frac23$ cup, and feeds $6\times8=48$ goldfish.

**Answer: (D) 48**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-27.title: Odd squares are odd
mathleague-2004-05-g8-27.body:
The square of an odd number is odd, so an integer whose square is even cannot be odd. (It can be prime: $2^2=4$; even: $4^2=16$; zero: $0^2=0$.)

**Answer: (B) odd**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-28.title: Simplify
mathleague-2004-05-g8-28.body:
The reciprocal of $\frac1{x^3}$ is $x^3$, so $4x=x^3$. Then $x=0$ or $x^2=4$, i.e. $x=\pm2$. The choice that works is 2.

**Answer: (C) 2**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-30.title: Convert seconds to days
mathleague-2004-05-g8-30.body:
$1\,000\,000\div60\div60\div24\approx11.57$ days. So the millionth second falls during the 12th day of the year, January 12.

**Answer: (B) January 12**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-32.title: Look at the product
mathleague-2004-05-g8-32.body:
The product's numerator is a product of even numbers, so it is even, and its denominator is a product of odd numbers, so it is odd. An even number divided by an odd number that gives an integer must be even (an odd divisor cannot cancel the factor 2).

**Answer: (A) even**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-33.title: Triangle inequality
mathleague-2004-05-g8-33.body:
We need $x<3+4=7$, so $x\le6$. The perimeter is at most $3+4+6=13$.

**Answer: (C) 13**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-35.title: Count the triangles
mathleague-2004-05-g8-35.body:
The figure has two sides meeting at the top and two lines crossing each other. Each of the two crossing lines cuts across both sides, giving 2 large triangles (a side pair plus one crossing line). The two crossing lines together with one side each form a small triangle on the left and on the right, giving 2 small triangles. Total $2+2=4$.

**Answer: (C) 4**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-36.title: Cancel opposites
mathleague-2004-05-g8-36.body:
The integers $-999,-998,\ldots,999,1000$ are 2000 consecutive integers; the numbers from $-999$ to $999$ cancel in pairs, leaving $1000$. Consecutive integers with a given sum are unique (shifting by 1 changes the sum by 2000), so the greatest is 1000, with digit sum $1$.

**Answer: (A) 1**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-37.title: List the factors
mathleague-2004-05-g8-37.body:
The factors divisible by 4 are 4, 8, 16, 20, 40, 80, 100, 200, 400: 9 of them.

**Answer: (C) 9**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-37.title: Prime factorization
mathleague-2004-05-g8-37.body:
$400=2^4\cdot5^2$. A factor divisible by 4 is $2^a5^b$ with $a\in\{2,3,4\}$ and $b\in\{0,1,2\}$: $3\times3=9$.

**Answer: (C) 9**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-39.title: Hour hand speed
mathleague-2004-05-g8-39.body:
The hour hand moves $30^\circ$ per hour, i.e. $0.5^\circ$ per minute. In 22 minutes after 12:00 it moves $22\times0.5=11^\circ$ from vertical.

**Answer: (B) $11^\circ$**

mathleague-2004-05-g8-40.title: Many factors of 10
mathleague-2004-05-g8-40.body:
The product contains the factors 10, 20, 30, $\ldots$, 90 and several 5s paired with 2s; in particular it is a multiple of $10\times20=200$, so it is divisible by 100. The last two digits are 00 and the tens' digit is 0.

**Answer: (D) 0**
